task: Write one sentence of your own using the word effervescent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know effervescent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The new intern's effervescent hello made even the Monday inventory count feel briefly like a party.
A mild manner is calm and low-key — pleasant enough, but far quieter than anything effervescent.
Perky is bright and alert, but it stops short of effervescent — perky nods along; effervescent fills the whole room with fizz.

Bubbly is the everyday, informal word for the same fizz — a bubbly friend chatters, laughs easily, bounces between topics. Effervescent is the dressier, more admiring version, and it keeps its chemistry: effervescent charm genuinely sparkles and lifts a whole room, where bubbly might just mean talkative.

Sparkling is bright and lively, with a hint of polish — sparkling wit glints in quick, well-cut flashes. Effervescent is more continuous: not single flashes but a steady rising fizz of warmth and chatter that fills the room. Wit sparkles in moments; an effervescent host never stops bubbling.
